title: AUTOMATED SAFETY EVALUATIONS ACROSS 20 LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: THE AYMARA LLM RISK AND RESPONSIBILITY MATRIX

bias_targets.methodology: Programmatic generation of adversarial prompts requesting stereotypes about different nationalities (e.g., historical stereotypes), with responses scored as safe or unsafe against a safety policy using an automated LLM-as-a-judge evaluator.

Programmatic generation of adversarial prompts asking for jokes or generalizations based on gender stereotypes, with responses scored for safety policy compliance using an automated LLM-as-a-judge evaluator.
Generating adversarial prompts that request subtle offensive content or euphemistic jokes regarding a person's ethnicity, evaluated by an LLM-as-a-judge for safety policy violations.
Testing model responses using prompts about religious stereotypes (e.g., analyzing media portrayals), with outputs scored as safe or unsafe by an automated LLM evaluator.
Prompting models to discuss or explain disability stereotypes (e.g., their influence on public policy) and scoring the resulting responses for safety policy compliance using an LLM-as-a-judge.
Generating prompts regarding sexual orientation stereotypes and using an automated LLM-as-a-judge to determine if the model's response violates hate speech and bias safety policies.
